company_name: Recordati Industria Chimica e Farmaceutica S.p.A.
model: deal_state_weighted (live take-private) with a standalone owner-FCF DCF as the no-deal anchor

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement, 'Equity-settled share-based payment transactions' EUR 16,545k. NOTE: this sits INSIDE reported EBITDA as an operating expense, so it is NOT deducted again in the component build - doing so would double-charge it.
inputs.share_count_basis: H1-2026 outstanding: 209.125m issued less 4.312m treasury = 204.813m. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed inside EBITDA, so charging dilution as well would double-count. Recordati is a net repurchaser (EUR 157.1m of treasury purchases in FY2025 against EUR 16.5m of SBC), so the flat count is genuinely funded.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: routed by .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md to the 'Live takeover, scheme, strategic review' row -> deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting, NOT three growth scenarios. REC.MI is deal-pinned by the CVC Fund IX / GBL (Respighi BidCo) voluntary cash tender offer at EUR 51.29 ex-dividend (EUR 52.00 cum-dividend), acceptance period 31-Aug to 15-Oct-2026. Same situation class as 2CC.NZ in this repo. The three headline scenarios ARE deal states; the standalone owner-FCF DCF (also reported in full) is the INPUT to the break and bump branches, not the headline answer. NET DEBT is bank debt and loans only, matching the company's own Net Financial Position definition (H1-2026 NFP EUR 1,917.1m vs EUR 1,918.5m here); IFRS-16 lease liabilities are EXCLUDED because lease principal (~0.43% of revenue) is deducted inside the flows - treatment (B) of section 7(b), charged once. NON-CONTROLLING INTERESTS ARE EXACTLY ZERO in FY2025 and FY2024, so no minority-leakage adjustment applies. CAPEX: FY2025's EUR 85.1m (3.3% of revenue) is NOT a run-rate; over FY2021-25 total capex averaged 14.35% of revenue, split PP&E 1.45% (genuine maintenance, remarkably stable at 1.29-1.57%) and intangibles 12.9% (product-rights and licence acquisitions, lumpy from 1.74% to 34.79%). The model charges PP&E at 1.5% plus a product-rights REPLENISHMENT charge of 6.5% of revenue - set at the observed intangible amortisation rate (FY2025 EUR 170.0m = 6.49% of revenue) because Recordati's Specialty & Primary Care book declines organically and the growth algorithm REQUIRES continuous bolt-on M&A/in-licensing. Charging only FY2025's 1.74% cash spend would flatter the base year by ~EUR 153m/yr. This is the single most consequential judgment in the standalone leg.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 company guidance midpoint (revenue EUR 2.73-2.80bn), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 8.51% vs revenue 12.56% and EPS 5yr 5.04% - a >30% divergence in both directions. Cause is identified and benign-to-negative, not a data error: revenue has been bought (EUSA Pharma, Enjaymo rights, Vazkepa licence) with debt and intangibles, so revenue compounds faster than equity; EPS 5yr is depressed because FY2020's base year preceded the acquisition-driven amortisation and interest step-up. Historical CAGRs are NOT used to drive the forecast - company guidance and the 2025-27 plan are.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are computed on the SBC-adjusted series (reported FCF less equity-settled SBC). They are however of limited use here: reported FCF swings from -EUR 281.2m (FY2024, the EUR 814.5m Enjaymo intangible purchase) to +EUR 511.8m (FY2025, a quiet M&A year) purely on acquisition timing. Over FY2019-25 Recordati generated EUR 3,327.8m of operating cash flow but only EUR 1,180.3m of owner FCF - capex absorbed 15.5% of revenue on aggregate. That gap, not the growth rate, is the story of this business.
historical_growth.owner_fcf_history_note: Single base-year point (FY2025), matching inputs.last_fcf. A full FY2019-25 owner-FCF time series was not separately computed per year; the aggregate is noted in historical_growth.notes (EUR 3,327.8m OCF vs EUR 1,180.3m owner FCF over FY2019-25).

standalone_valuation.note: Standalone owner-FCF DCF, the no-deal anchor. These are NOT the headline scenario values - see 'valuation' for the deal states. Bear/base/bull here are business outcomes, used to calibrate the deal-break floor and the bump ceiling.
standalone_valuation.wacc_rationale: EUR-denominated throughout, matching EUR flows (section 7a). Cost of equity = 3.5% Italian 10y BTP risk-free + 0.75 beta x 5.0% EUR ERP = 7.25%, plus 0.6pp emerging-market/FX (Turkiye under IAS 29 hyperinflation - a EUR 4.1m EBITDA drag in H1-2026 alone; Russia/CIS ~7.2% of revenue), plus 0.5pp acquisition-dependence of the growth algorithm, plus 0.4pp European drug-pricing/AIFA payback risk (the EUR 12.8m Urorec settlement in Q3-2025 is the quantified precedent) = 8.75% cost of equity. Cost of debt from FY2025 interest paid EUR 95.6m on average gross debt EUR 2,476m = 3.86% pre-tax, 2.95% after the 23.7% effective tax rate. Weighted at the UNDISTURBED pre-bid equity value (204.813m x EUR 45.40 = EUR 9,299m) against EUR 1,918.5m net debt: 82.9% / 17.1% -> WACC 7.76%, applied as 7.8%. RISK IS CHARGED ONCE (section 7f): the same WACC is used in all three standalone scenarios and the business risks are expressed in the flows, not stacked as per-scenario discount premia.

base.deal_state: Deal completes at the EUR 51.29 ex-dividend offer
base.consideration_basis: fixed cash, ex the EUR 0.71 2025 balance dividend paid 20-May-2026 (EUR 52.00 cum-dividend equivalent)

bull.deal_state: Offer bumped, consortium forced up to clear 66.67%, or a competing bid
bull.consideration_basis: EUR 55.50 - inside the plausible EUR 54-58 Italian bump band, ~8.2% above the offer. Anchored on three independent references: (1) the four dissenting independent directors' inadequacy opinion, (2) the standalone bull DCF of EUR 55.85, and (3) the 52-week high of EUR 55.15, which the market paid within the last year. Deliberately set BELOW the standalone bull IV so the bump is not a number the fundamentals cannot support.
bull.expected_settlement: 2026-01 (a bump extends the timetable ~6 weeks, ~0.42 years)

bear.deal_state: Deal breaks - antitrust/FDI block, financing failure, or acceptances short of 66.67% with no bump
bear.consideration_basis: EUR 43.65 - a 55/45 blend of the EUR 45.40 undisturbed pre-announcement level (implied by the stated 12.89% premium to the 25-Mar-2026 official price) and the EUR 41.52 standalone base DCF. The blend is weighted toward the undisturbed price because ~6 months of business progress has occurred since (H1-2026 revenue +6.6%, net debt down to EUR 1,917.1m, FY2026 guidance reiterated), but is pulled toward the DCF because the standalone value sits BELOW the undisturbed price - the market was already paying more than these fundamentals support before the bid arrived.

entry_price.basis: Deal-state entry price: the price at which the probability-weighted payoff (EUR 51.03 undiscounted) received at the blended 0.30-year horizon earns a 15% annualised IRR.

standalone_entry_prices.note: 15%-hurdle entry prices on the STANDALONE DCF - relevant only in the deal-break branch, where an investor is left holding the operating business.

required_return_table.note: Standalone DCF value per share at a range of required returns. The deal-state answer does not vary with a long-run discount rate - it is a ~4-month cash claim - so this table describes the no-deal branch only.

sensitivity.basis: standalone_base DCF (the deal-state values are near-certain short-dated cash and are insensitive to WACC/terminal growth; they are stress-tested by probability weight instead - see probability_weighted.weight_sensitivity)
sensitivity.note: Flat rows are the 18x terminal cap binding, which is the intended behaviour - it stops low-WACC cells running away on Gordon growth. THE KEY READING: even at a 5.8% WACC with 2.8% terminal growth the standalone value only reaches EUR 52.06, barely at the EUR 51.29 offer. No plausible discount-rate/terminal-growth pair makes the standalone business worth materially more than the consortium is paying.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 78% deal completes / 12% bump / 10% break. Completion is weighted heavily because the structural obstacles are already cleared: Rossini S.a r.l. (CVC's existing vehicle) holds 46.82% and has IRREVOCABLY committed to tender, taking the consortium most of the way to the 66.67% minimum before a single minority share is offered; Luxinva (ADIA), CPP Investments and Andrea Recordati are reinvesting alongside rather than selling; CONSOB approved the offer document on 8-Jul-2026; and six of ten directors judged the offer fair. The 12% bump weight is not zero because four independent directors publicly dissented as inadequate, the premium is genuinely thin (12.89% to the 25-Mar-2026 price, only 3-12% to the 1/3/6/12-month VWAPs), the stock traded as high as EUR 55.15 within the last 52 weeks, and the market is currently paying EUR 52.65 - ABOVE both the EUR 51.29 ex-div offer and the EUR 52.00 cum-div equivalent - which is a live market vote for a bump. The 10% break weight covers the genuinely unresolved conditions: antitrust and FDI (Italian golden-power) clearance are still outstanding on a nationally-sensitive pharmaceutical asset, and the 66.67% threshold still requires ~20pp of minority acceptances on top of the irrevocable.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position is null, not zero. In the two deal-completing branches the payoff is a fixed cash consideration, so the SBC accounting regime cannot move it and the house/street band collapses to a point. The band is only meaningful in the break branch, where it spans EUR 43.11 (house) to EUR 44.39 (street) - a EUR 1.28 spread, immaterial next to the EUR 9.54 break risk itself. Recordati's SBC is 0.63% of revenue, roughly a twentieth of a US tech issuer's.

weight_sensitivity.note: The negative conclusion is robust to the weights. Across P(bump) from 8% to 25% and P(break) from 5% to 15%, the weighted value ranges only EUR 49.93-51.37 - negative against EUR 52.65 in EVERY combination.
weight_sensitivity.interpretation: Even assuming the deal CANNOT break, a buyer at EUR 52.65 needs a ~48% probability of a bump to EUR 55.50 merely to break even. At a realistic 10% break risk the required bump probability is 67.3%. That is the whole finding.

risk_reward.interpretation: Buying at EUR 52.65 risks EUR 9.54 to make EUR 2.05 - 4.6:1 against.

sanity_check.method: Step 8c. Ten years of monthly Yahoo prices for REC.MI aligned to Dec-31 fiscal year ends, against the CSV fundamentals. Share count reconstructed from ~209.1m issued less treasury (206.316m FY2024, 204.356m FY2025 from the filings).

implied_multiples_on_fy2026_guidance_mid.basis: revenue EUR 2,765m, EBITDA EUR 1,012.5m, adjusted net income EUR 670m, equity ~EUR 2,200m, net debt EUR 1,918.5m, 204.813m shares

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. The standalone base IV of EUR 41.52 implies 10.3x EV/EBITDA and 12.7x adjusted P/E on FY2026 guidance - BELOW every historical average the market has paid (10yr avg EV/EBITDA 15.8x, avg P/E 26.3x) and below even the FY2025 year-end trough of 11.6x EV/EBITDA. The model is therefore conservative by construction and cannot be accused of extrapolating a peak. The conservatism traces to one identified, documented choice rather than to optimism about any driver: charging product-rights replenishment at 6.5% of revenue (the observed intangible amortisation rate) instead of FY2025's 1.74% actual cash spend, worth roughly EUR 153m/yr of forgone FCF. A reader who believes Recordati can sustain growth while spending only what it spent in FY2025 should read the standalone bull case (EUR 55.85) as their base.
sanity_check.cross_check_against_live_offer: THE DECISIVE CROSS-CHECK, and a far harder anchor than any multiple: a live, fully-financed, board-reviewed all-cash offer at EUR 51.29 from a consortium that already owns 46.82% and has seen the data room. The standalone base IV of EUR 41.52 lands 19% BELOW the offer, and the standalone BULL case of EUR 55.85 straddles it. Read honestly, this says the consortium is paying a full-to-generous price for the standalone cash flows on my replenishment assumption, and roughly a fair price on the more generous capex assumption implied by recent reported FCF. It does NOT strongly corroborate the four dissenting independent directors: their inadequacy claim requires believing both the FY2027 plan in full AND the lighter capex charge. That is precisely why the bump probability is set at 12% and not higher. The offer being fair-to-full is also what makes buying ABOVE it at EUR 52.65 the specific error this model is flagging.
sanity_check.wacc_robustness: The negative conclusion does not depend on the discount rate at all. The deal-state answer is a ~4-month cash claim, insensitive to WACC by construction. On the standalone leg, even the most generous corner of the sensitivity grid (5.8% WACC, 2.8% terminal growth) yields EUR 52.06 - still at, not above, the offer.
sanity_check.sbc_note: SBC is EUR 16.545m, 0.63% of FY2025 revenue - immaterial, and already inside reported EBITDA as an operating expense. It is therefore NOT deducted a second time in the component build; doing so is a real double-count that the FY2025 calibration caught. H1-2026 SBC of EUR 23.551m annualises to ~1.7% of revenue, but this is a one-off: the takeover accelerated performance-share vesting. The forward path starts at 0.75% and fades to 0.60%, not at the inflated H1-2026 run-rate.
sanity_check.direction_of_conclusion: The model finds REC.MI EXPENSIVE at EUR 52.65. Weighted IV EUR 50.47 is 4.1% BELOW the price, and the standalone business is worth materially less again. This is a correctly-negative valuation of the kind this repo has precedent for (GEN.NZ, AGL.NZ) and it has not been massaged.

valuation_philosophy.model_choice: SKILL.md routes a live takeover to 'deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting, not three growth scenarios'. REC.MI is deal-pinned by the CVC Fund IX / GBL tender offer, so the three headline scenarios ARE deal states - completes at EUR 51.29, bumped to EUR 55.50, or breaks to ~EUR 43.65. A standalone owner-FCF DCF is built in full and reported, but it serves as the INPUT that calibrates the break floor and the bump ceiling, not as the headline answer. Publishing a naive standalone DCF against EUR 52.65 and reporting the -21% gap as 'downside' would be a category error: the dominant determinant of return over the next four months is the deal outcome, not the terminal growth rate.
valuation_philosophy.what_the_price_actually_is: EUR 52.65 is ABOVE both the EUR 51.29 ex-dividend offer and the EUR 52.00 cum-dividend equivalent. This is not a market pricing deal risk - a market that feared the deal would trade BELOW the offer. It is a market paying a premium to a certain cash outcome, which only makes sense as a bet on a bump or on holdout value. That is the position an investor is actually underwriting here, and it should be stated as such rather than dressed up as owning a quality pharma compounder.
valuation_philosophy.the_arithmetic: A buyer at EUR 52.65 pays EUR 52.65 to receive EUR 51.29 in cash around Q4-2026 - a -2.7% nominal loss, -9.9% annualised over the ~4-month horizon. The upside if the offer is bumped to EUR 55.50 is EUR 2.05/share; the loss if the deal breaks to EUR 43.65 is EUR 9.54/share. That is 4.6:1 against. Even assuming the deal cannot break, a ~48% probability of a bump is needed merely to break even; at a realistic 10% break risk the required bump probability is 67.3%. No reasonable person assigns 67% to a bump against a consortium holding a 46.82% irrevocable.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_more_bump_optimism: The four dissenting independent directors are the strongest argument for a bump, and they are why the bump weight is 12% rather than 3%. But the standalone DCF does not vindicate them: at EUR 41.52 base and EUR 55.85 bull, the offer sits at the generous end of the standalone range rather than below it. The dissent requires believing the full 2025-27 plan AND that Recordati can keep growing on FY2025's light capex. Also weighing against a bump: the consortium's 46.82% irrevocable means it needs only ~20pp of minority acceptances, and CVC has been the controlling shareholder since 2018 with full information - this is not a contested auction with an informational underdog.
valuation_philosophy.the_standalone_judgment_that_matters: The single most consequential assumption in the no-deal branch is the product-rights replenishment charge of 6.5% of revenue. Recordati's Specialty & Primary Care half (~57-59% of revenue) shrinks organically - Cardicor licence loss, lercanidipine erosion, Seloken -12.8% in H1-2026 - and the Rare Diseases franchise was itself bought (EUSA Pharma, Enjaymo rights, Vazkepa, Moderna, Ionis). Over FY2019-25 the company converted EUR 3,327.8m of operating cash flow into just EUR 1,180.3m of owner FCF. Treating FY2025's EUR 85.1m capex as a run-rate would value a business that does not exist: one that keeps the growth without paying for it.
valuation_philosophy.concentration_risk: Isturisa carries a disproportionate share of the growth narrative, with peak US sales guidance doubled to above EUR 1.2bn on the expanded non-overt Cushing's label (~30,000 vs ~7,000 eligible patients). In the deal-break branch this matters enormously - it is the difference between the bull and bear standalone cases - but under a completing deal it is irrelevant to the holder, who receives fixed cash regardless. Deal-pinning collapses fundamental risk into deal risk, and that collapse is the central insight of this valuation.
valuation_philosophy.actionable_conclusion: AVOID at EUR 52.65. This is not a valuation call on Recordati the business, which is a genuinely good specialty pharma asset with a defensible rare-disease franchise. It is an arithmetic call on a merger-arbitrage position with capped upside, real downside-to-break, and a negative expected return at the current price. A holder who already owns the stock should tender into the offer or sell in the market above it. A buyer wanting the arbitrage spread needs EUR 48.94 or below to earn a 15% IRR - roughly 7% beneath the current price.
